question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Pulse-chase decoupling of AP-1 establishment from maintenance
ideas.description: Use an optogenetic or chemically inducible AP-1 construct (plus a degron on endogenous Jun/Fos family members) to deliver a defined transient pulse, then chase for many days and track target-gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Depleting AP-1 at staggered times after the pulse distinguishes whether AP-1 is only needed to write the state or is continuously required to hold it — the key discriminator between a memory mechanism and a simple persistent signal.

ideas.title: Lineage-barcoded sister-cell concordance of AP-1 target states
ideas.description: Barcode single cells and profile single-cell RNA plus ATAC after several divisions, quantifying how much more similar AP-1 target expression and AP-1 motif accessibility are between clonal relatives than between unrelated cells, as a function of generations since the common ancestor. The decay of this concordance gives a direct, quantitative memory half-life in cell divisions rather than in hours.

ideas.title: Hysteresis mapping of AP-1 dose-response
ideas.description: Expose cells to graded stimulus levels on both an ascending and a descending ramp and read out AP-1 activity with a live reporter at single-cell resolution. A reproducible gap between the up and down curves is the classic signature of a bistable, self-reinforcing circuit, and its absence would argue AP-1 is relaying rather than storing information.

ideas.title: Sort-and-regrow stability assay on an endogenous AP-1 reporter
ideas.description: Knock a fluorescent reporter into an endogenous AP-1 target locus, sort the top and bottom expression deciles, regrow each population, and measure how quickly the full distribution is regenerated. The relaxation timescale, compared with cell-cycle time and mRNA/protein half-lives, reveals whether the state is heritably locked or merely slow-fluctuating noise.

ideas.title: Prime-and-challenge transcriptional priming with enhancer dissection
ideas.description: Prime cells with a stimulus, wait until AP-1 protein and target transcripts return to baseline, then rechallenge and measure the speed and amplitude of the nascent transcriptional response. CRISPR deletion of individual AP-1-bound enhancers, and a heterologous second stimulus, then test whether the stored memory is localized to specific elements and whether it is stimulus-specific or general.

candidates: Lineage-barcoded sister-cell analysis to test whether AP-1 target gene states are shared across sibling cells for multiple generations
Live imaging of endogenously tagged c-Jun/FOSL1 with an AP-1 synthetic reporter to measure autocorrelation time of AP-1 activity along lineage trees
Transient optogenetic or degron pulse of AP-1 followed by long chase to test persistence of transcriptional state after the input is removed
Single-cell ATAC time course after a transient stimulus to ask whether AP-1 motif accessibility remains elevated long after AP-1 protein decays
Cell sorting on an AP-1 activity reporter, then regrowth and re-measurement to test whether high and low states regenerate the parental distribution or persist
Degron-mediated acute AP-1 depletion at defined times after priming to test whether AP-1 is required for maintenance versus only establishment of the state
CUT&RUN for AP-1 factors plus pioneer partners across a time course to see whether AP-1 occupancy is self-sustaining at primed enhancers
Test for an AP-1 transcriptional autoregulatory loop by measuring nascent transcription of JUN/FOS family genes at their own motif-bound enhancers
Mathematical bistability test: dose-response hysteresis of AP-1 activity to graded stimulus up and down ramps
Single-molecule RNA FISH of AP-1 targets in clonal populations to quantify heritable versus transient cell-to-cell variability
Measure whether AP-1-dependent enhancer states survive mitosis via mitotic bookmarking assays (chromosome spreads, mitotic CUT&RUN)
Nucleosome turnover and histone exchange measurements at AP-1 enhancers to test whether memory is chromatin-stabilized
Serial restimulation assay measuring faster or larger transcriptional response on second exposure (transcriptional priming) and its AP-1 dependence
CRISPR deletion of individual AP-1-bound enhancers to test whether specific elements store the memory of prior stimulus
Prime-and-challenge with heterologous stimuli to test whether AP-1 memory is stimulus-general or stimulus-specific
Single-cell multiome (RNA plus ATAC) with clone barcodes to link heritable accessibility states to heritable expression states
Proteomic measurement of AP-1 dimer composition over time to test whether a switch in dimer identity encodes the memory
Dilution-of-label experiments (e.g., SNAP-tag pulse labeling) to measure AP-1 protein inheritance and partitioning at division
Drug-tolerant persister resensitization assay testing whether AP-1 activity predicts and is required for reversible drug tolerance memory
Synthetic reconstitution: insert isolated AP-1 binding sites at a reporter locus and ask if the reporter alone shows heritable bimodal states
Comparative cross-species or cross-cell-type analysis of AP-1 motif accessibility persistence to test generality
Perturb-seq of chromatin regulators in AP-1-primed cells to find the factors required for state maintenance
Measure memory decay half-life as a function of cell cycle arrest to separate dilution from active erasure
